title: How many jobs should the print shop plan for?

beats.say: The print shop opens at eight. How much work should we leave room for?
This ticket sets tomorrow’s capacity. We want enough room for nine mornings out of ten.
Picture ten equally likely mornings at the shop. Each stack is one possible queue. Each sheet is one job.
Nine stacks have ten jobs apiece.
Where’s the lowest setting that covers nine mornings?
Try nine jobs. Even the short stacks stick out above the rail.
Lift it one sheet. Now all nine fit.
Ten jobs is the first setting that covers ninety percent. That’s the ninetieth percentile, or P ninety.
Now change one morning. A school sends over a poster run. That stack grows from ten jobs to forty.
Leave the rail at ten. How many mornings still fit?
Eight. The poster order is sticking out.
Raise the rail until that order almost clears. At thirty-nine jobs, the top sheet is still above it.
One more. Forty. The ninth stack fits again.
The hundred-job morning never changed. The ninth stack did. Write forty jobs on tomorrow’s ticket.
